teams.heading: Fiji sit bottom of the Nations Championship after conceding 145 points
teams.body: Fiji occupy the bottom spot in the Nations Championship table following three consecutive defeats at the start of their campaign. The Flying Fijians have struggled for defensive solidity, conceding 145 points while scoring only 49 across their opening three fixtures — including a 17-33 loss to Scotland last time out. This difficult run of form stands in stark contrast to the heights of 2023, when the national side achieved their highest ever world ranking of No. 7.

teams.body: Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter has confirmed that tight-head prop Josh Iosefa-Scott is likely to move to France when his contract expires next summer. While acknowledging that the English-qualified forward has received a significant offer from a French club, Baxter clarified that no specific destination has been confirmed. The Exeter boss expressed a pragmatic view on the departure, stating, "I haven't had any confirmation of whatever club he's going to," while praising the player's consistent performances for the Chiefs.

teams.body: Former Munster captain Peter O’Mahony has revealed that Rassie Erasmus’ 2017 exit to join SA Rugby left him deeply disappointed at the time. O’Mahony, writing in his book All In, explained that he felt the team was finally gaining necessary direction under the South African’s guidance. While the flanker acknowledged the ruthless nature of professional sport and admitted he would likely have made the same choice himself, he conceded that the loss of Erasmus was a difficult moment for the squad.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie backs NPC importance amid national competition structural overhaul talks
teams.body: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has emphasised that the NPC must remain central to the national rugby landscape. Amid discussions regarding potential domestic reforms—including possible Super Rugby expansion or an entirely new 8-10 team competition—Rennie described the NPC as a vital part of the nation's "rugby fabric". The coach insisted the competition is essential for player development, noting: "It's a real point of difference from a World Rugby perspective; I reckon it's the greatest provincial competition in the world."

teams.body: Former Munster captain Peter O'Mahony has opened up about the impact of Rassie Erasmus’s exit from the Irish province in 2017. Reflecting on their time together in his new book, O'Mahony admitted he felt "hurt" when the director of rugby left for his role with South Africa. Despite the professional disappointment, O'Mahony acknowledged that returning home to lead the national team was a logical step for Erasmus, who subsequently guided the Springboks to two World Cup titles.
